legend: The Jiangshi, the hopping corpse (China, Qing dynasty folklore)
lines: Hunan, China, long ago. Rain falls on a mountain road.
A traveler hears a slow, strange thump. Thump. Thump.
Out of the mist hops a stiff figure with its arms stretched out.
A yellow paper charm is stuck to its forehead.
Legend says this is a jiangshi, a hopping corpse.
It cannot see you, but it can feel your breath.
So the traveler hides in an inn and holds his breath.
The thing hops closer and closer, then stops at the door.
At dawn, the rooster crows, and the hopping stops.
Could you hold your breath that long?
title: The Jiangshi: China's Hopping Corpse That Hunts by Your Breath #shorts
description:
In old Chinese folklore, the jiangshi is a stiff, hopping corpse with a paper charm on its forehead. Legend says it hunts by feeling your breath.
